page: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 96 dedicated vCPUs spanning 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory capacity is substantial at 768 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The processor architecture incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction support for AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Bundled local storage includes 5669 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD capacity, while discrete GPU acceleration is not present.

Benchmark results validate strong multi-core computational throughput and exceptional memory subsystems. The instance scored 93,126.45 on the PassMark CPU test and achieved 87,583.29 in multi-core stress-ng tests. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 506.7 GB/s and write bandwidth achieved 207.77 GB/s, both landing within the top tier of evaluated hardware. Database and I/O workloads demonstrate significant efficiency, reflected by 35,335.9 PassMark database operations and 122.52 million Redis SET operations per second. Static web serving throughput also measured in the top tier at 136.17 GB/s.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E96ds_v6 offers high resource density by combining large RAM capacity with extensive bundled NVMe storage on a single node, reducing the need to provision separate dedicated storage instances. The lack of integrated GPU hardware means vector and inference tasks rely on CPU extensions like AMX, showing robust prompt-processing throughput but moderate per-token generation speeds. The server is well matched for large in-memory databases, real-time analytics, caching tiers, enterprise relational database systems, and heavy ETL pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v6 is an enterprise memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs from a 48-core Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 768 GB of system memory, the instance delivers an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, supported by 260 MB of L3 cache and AMX matrix instructions. It integrates 5669 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage with zero discrete GPUs. Performance benchmarks show top-tier results in uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 506 GB/s read, top-tier database operations, and high multi-core execution in PassMark and stress-ng tests. The consolidated high-density memory and fast local disk provide favorable operational efficiency for data-intensive infrastructure, making this instance suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, high-volume transactional databases, and demanding analytical data pipelines.
